tip: Gerunds ending in -в mark an action finished before the main verb: Подумав (podumav = having thought), then agreeing.
Gerunds ending in -я show action at the same time as the main verb: Работая (rabotaya = working) while he saves time.
Reflexive verbs ending in -ся build the gerund with -вшись: Вернувшись (vernuvshis = having returned).
A few verbs form the -я gerund irregularly, giving Лёжа (lyozha = lying) instead of the regular lezha form.
In passives the doer goes in the instrumental case: учёным (uchyonym = by a scientist) after изобретено (izobreteno = invented).
Short passive participles agree like adjectives: places are plural, so заняты (zanyaty = taken) takes the plural -ы ending.
Adding -ся makes an ongoing passive with no named doer: обновляется (obnovlyaetsya = is being updated) needs no 'by whom'.
Future passive uses будут (budut = will be) plus a short participle: будут объявлены (budut obyavleny = will be announced).
Collective numerals like Двое (dvoe = two) count groups of people and take the genitive plural: Двое детей (dvoe detey = two children).
Оба (oba = both) takes the genitive singular noun, same as 2 to 4: Оба брата (oba brata = both brothers), not the plural.
After 2, 3, 4 the noun is genitive singular: Четыре месяца (chetyre mesyatsa = four months), never the plural form.
Полтора (poltora = one and a half) is followed by the genitive singular: Полтора часа (poltora chasa = an hour and a half).
In compound ordinals only the final word changes: Двадцать первый (dvadtsat pervyy = twenty-first) puts the ending on the last part.
Good wishes drop 'I wish you' and put the noun in the genitive: Хорошего вечера (khoroshego vechera = good evening).
The position word до (do = until) takes the genitive: До встречи (do vstrechi = until the meeting), the usual way to say see you.
Apologies use за (za = for) plus the accusative: Извините за беспокойство (izvinite za bespokoystvo = sorry for the trouble).
After a measure word the substance goes in the genitive: литр молока (litr moloka = a liter of milk), showing the amount.
A plain they-form with no subject means 'will be done': построят (postroyat = they will build) reads as a bridge will be built.
Не за что (ne za chto = don't mention it) is the set reply to thanks, literally 'there is nothing to thank for'.
After numbers грамм often keeps its short genitive plural: двести грамм (dvesti gramm = two hundred grams) in everyday speech.
